summary: No region-specific signal was identified for Arauca department: the sources assembled for this record contain no Arauca-specific legal, enforcement or incident finding, and the national assessment carried in the parent record applies.
tangentialFactors:
The two sources reviewed for Arauca document events in other Colombian departments, one concerning a killing in Bello, Antioquia and the other armed-group threat campaigns in Caquetá. Neither reports any occurrence, order or practice located in Arauca, so the material establishes the national pattern of targeted violence against trans people without speaking to conditions in this department.

The Caquetá investigation is the closer comparison for Arauca: both are eastern departments with a documented armed-group presence, and the tactics it records, named kill lists circulated on flyers and WhatsApp, ultimatums to leave town, and displacement of trans women from ordinary work, are the specific mechanisms a visitor would want confirmed or excluded for Arauca. The sources do not confirm or exclude them here.
localsOnly: No resident-facing facts specific to Arauca were sourced. Nothing in the inventory addresses how the department's notaries, police, health facilities or detaining authorities handle trans residents, nor whether local armed groups have issued threats naming trans people in Arauca.
outOfScopeNotes: Unresolved: whether threat campaigns of the kind documented in Caquetá and Guajira operate in Arauca is not sourced either way, and the absence of reporting should not be read as absence of activity. The inventory also provides nothing on Arauca-specific enforcement of access-to-premises rulings, on the treatment of trans detainees in the department's facilities, or on the availability of hormone therapy and other trans-related care locally. National figures on killings of trans people are reported without a departmental breakdown, so Arauca's share cannot be determined.
